Ted Brown

Libertarian candidate for U.S. Senator, Texas · Open seat

Retired independent insurance adjuster

Ted Brown is the Libertarian Party nominee for U.S. Senate in Texas. He joined the Libertarian Party in 1979, chaired the Libertarian Party of California, and is now vice chair of the Libertarian Party of Travis County. He was the party's 2024 nominee for U.S. Senate in Texas and received more than 267,000 votes, a record for a Libertarian Senate candidate in the state.

Where Brown stands

Gas tax
Would repeal the federal gas tax entirely.
Data centers
Generally opposes regulation, but sees merit in requiring power and water plans and in banning taxpayer subsidies and eminent domain for data centers.
Iran and war powers
Supports every war powers resolution and wants U.S. troops withdrawn from the Middle East. Proposes withdrawing the U.S. from foreign conflicts and alliances, including NATO.
Border wall in Big Bend
Wants Congress to bar a wall in Big Bend and to stop further border wall construction.
Gender care for minors
Says the government has no place in medical decisions between doctors and patients and argues the issue is overblown. Does not advocate surgery for minors.
Marijuana and hemp
Wants cannabis removed from federal drug scheduling and past marijuana convictions expunged.
Tariffs
Says only Congress can set tariffs; supports free trade.
Taxes and spending
Proposes abolishing the federal income tax, the IRS and the Department of Education, and making deep spending cuts to address the national debt.
Immigration
Proposes an Ellis Island-style legal immigration system.
Gun rights
Describes himself as a strong supporter of Second Amendment gun rights.

Background

  • Libertarian nominee, U.S. Senate, Texas, 2024 (more than 267,000 votes)
  • Vice chair, Libertarian Party of Travis County
  • Candidate coordinator, Libertarian Party of Texas; member, Texas State Libertarian Executive Committee
  • Former chair, Libertarian Party of California; former member, Libertarian National Committee
  • Member of the Libertarian Party since 1979
  • Independent, self-employed insurance adjuster (retired)
  • B.A. in political science, UCLA, 1984
